newsitem.title: UK: Euro fuel barges ease, but cargoes firmer.
newsitem.headline: Euro fuel barges ease, but cargoes firmer.

text.p: European high sulphur barges eased slightly on Monday, following crude's recent fall and with low bunker demand, while cargoes moved higher due to a shortage of sellers, traders said. High sulphur fuel oil barges traded at $85.50 and $85 a tonne fob Rotterdam after one deal at $86 earlier, which was $1.50 under Friday's highest trade. Some traders, saying buyers were later bidding $82/$83 and sellers $4 to $5 higher, said that they were seeing an end to high sulphur's recent big gains after crude's fall on Frirday.
"We have seen very few bunker enquiries, I think that's the reason for the lower prices, plus crude is coming down," a trader said.
"The general expectation is that it will fall further tomorrow unless we get a tremendous amount of enquiries again but I doubt that as we have seen a lot already last week," the trader added.
A high sulphur cargo loading June 20-30 was heard bought by trader from a U.K. major at $81.75 fob Coryton, a price deemed high by some traders.
"I am surprised at the strength shown by high sulphur (cargoes) with crude falling...I suspect the buyer could not find other sellers," one trader said.

One percent was steady in a quiet market although swaps came off a little to about $92 a tonne. Physical prices held. "We've got nothing prompt but something later in the month, but with the market so quiet and not interested buyers nothing could be gained from offering a cargo," one trader said, adding he would offer "theoretically" at about $93.50 to $94 a tonne. --Haitham Haddadin, London newsroom +44 171 542 8145
